description:
Krittin Kawkeeree, who was born in Thailand, developed a keen interest in robotics at the National University of Singapore and got into developing autonomous navigation systems for robots. Singaporean technopreneur Chinn Lim meanwhile had ambitions for his AI robotics start-up, dConstruct – but struggled to compete with big companies for the small pool of local talent.

Krittin was the missing piece to his dream. Since joining dConstruct in 2021, he has created the foundational systems for its products. Take the d.ASH Pack, a portable tool that collects data for 3D mapping for autonomous navigation. He also mentors and trains local interns to become full-time engineers with dConstruct.

(Video produced in partnership with the Ministry of Manpower.) 

00:00 Meet d.ASH-ER, the autonomous multitasking robot 
00:46 From Silicon Valley to masters degree at NUS 
01:15 Why a start-up struggles to hire local talent 
02:19 Why Krittin was a game-changer for dConstruct 
03:10 Turing interns into AI robotics engineers
07:01 Singapore’s COMPASS points-based system for hiring foreigners
09:11 Krittin’s hopes for the future 

COMPASS, the Complementarity Assessment Framework, was introduced by the government to help companies select a high-quality workforce while improving workforce diversity and building a strong local core.
